headline: Pricing discipline offsets energy inflation, outlook holds
summary_short: Vulcan reported Q2 2026 revenue of $2,155.8M (+2.5% y/y) and net earnings attributable to Vulcan of $323.4M (+0.8% y/y, $2.48 diluted EPS), while Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed 110bp y/y to 30.3% on energy cost inflation.
summary_long: Aggregates freight-adjusted pricing rose 5% y/y (mix-adjusted) and shipments grew 1%, lifting cash gross profit per ton to $12.02 despite diesel-driven cost inflation (cash cost of sales +7% y/y, +3% ex-diesel) and weather disruption in Texas and the Southeast. Consolidated gross profit was flat y/y as Asphalt/Concrete profit fell after the Houston asphalt and California ready-mix divestitures. SAG fell 2% y/y to $141M. Diluted EPS rose 2.5% y/y to $2.48 on net income growth and a lower share count. The Company returned $318M to shareholders ($250M buybacks, $68M dividends) and reiterated full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.4-2.6B (midpoint $2.5B). Debt/TTM EBITDA improved to 1.9x from 2.2x.

drivers.explanation: CEO Pruitt attributed the quarter to commercial and operational execution amid energy inflation and disruptive weather; aggregates cash gross profit per ton grew to over $12, and portfolio actions (California ready-mix divestiture, Colorado quarry and Dallas-Fort Worth rail yard acquisitions) advanced the aggregates-led growth strategy.

Aggregates freight-adjusted selling prices rose 5% on a mix-adjusted basis y/y (4%, or $0.86/ton, reported) while shipments grew 1%, though Texas and Southeastern volumes were hit by significant May-June rainfall.

Aggregates segment gross profit rose to $567M ($9.47/ton) on pricing and cost discipline, but this was offset at the consolidated level by lower Asphalt and Concrete gross profit following the Houston asphalt and California ready-mix divestitures.

Adjusted EBITDA margin fell 110bp y/y to 30.3% as freight-adjusted cash cost of sales rose 7% ($0.72/ton) on higher diesel fuel costs; excluding diesel, cash costs rose only 3%, reflecting continued cost-management focus.

Table A shows the y/y GAAP operating-earnings decline is explained by a swing to an $11.3M net loss on asset/business sales (from a $1.2M gain) and higher other operating expense, which outweighed a 2% SAG reduction.
Mirrors the Operating income decline described above; both track the same y/y GAAP operating-earnings move disclosed in Table A.

Net earnings grew slightly y/y as revenue growth and a 2% SAG reduction offset higher cost of revenue and other operating expense; income tax expense also fell to $81.4M from $91.3M as the effective tax rate declined to 20.1% from 22.0%.
Diluted EPS rose in line with net income growth, aided by a reduction in diluted share count (130.3M vs 132.9M y/y) from continued buybacks — $250M of stock repurchased in the quarter.
